# Seloger.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/seloger-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/seloger-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects real estate data from seloger.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Seloger.com - Real Estate Listing Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-seloger-com-listing-real-estate-ads)
- **Code:** [`seloger.py`](seloger.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Property pages](results/property.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Seloger search for finding property listings
- Seloger propery pages for property data

## Functions

- `scrape_search(url, max_pages=10)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape seloger search pages, which supports pagination by adding a LISTING-LISTpg parameter at the end of the URL https://www.seloger.com/classified-search?distributionTypes=Buy&estateTypes=Apartment&locations=AD08FR13100&page=page_number
- `scrape_property(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape seloger property pages

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import seloger


async def main():
    search = await seloger.scrape_search(
        url="https://www.seloger.com/classified-search?distributionTypes=Buy&estateTypes=Apartment&locations=AD08FR13100",
        max_pages=2,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/property.json`](results/property.json): `brand`, `id`, `metadata`, `domains`, `sections`, `contactSections`, `tracking`, `legacyTracking`, `advertising`, `seo`, `farbwelt`, `defaultBackToSearch`, `tags`, `rawData`, `aiEnrichments`, `correlationId`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `title`, `url`, `images`, `price`, `price_per_m2`, `property_facts`, `address`, `agency`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`seloger.py`](seloger.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"fr"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/seloger-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_search_scraping`, `test_property_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
